source.title: The Effects of Dapagliflozin in Patients With Heart Failure Complicated With Type 2 Diabetes: A Meta-Analysis of Placebo-Controlled Randomized Trials

duplicate_review.finding: All atom_id values are unique. Similar endpoint atoms were retained only where the source itself reports materially conflicting values (for example, abstract versus main-text HFrEF results and prose versus Figure 3C all-cause mortality).

findings: The pooled total of 5,252 is arithmetically consistent with using 2,139 diabetic participants from McMurray 2019, but the next Results sentence states 2,319; Table 1 lists the full McMurray trial arms (2,373 + 2,371 = 4,744).
Figure 3C reports pooled all-cause mortality OR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66-0.94), while the Results prose and abstract report OR 0.76 with the same interval.

The abstract reports HFrEF cardiovascular-death I²=8% and all-cause-mortality OR 0.70 (95% CI 0.50-0.99; I²=43%); the main Results text/Figure 4 report CVD I²=0% and ACM OR 0.69 (95% CI 0.53-0.89; I²=16%).
Figure 1's PRISMA flow shows 21 records screened and 5 studies included, but the intermediate 'reports sought for retrieval' and 'reports assessed for eligibility' boxes are both labeled n=0.
The Discussion says two trials had >1,000 participants and 'the other four trials' had <1,000 participants despite only five trials being included.

schema_gaps: The LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated systematic-review/meta-analysis atom kind. Review methods, pooled estimates, evidence-quality statements, source inconsistencies, and author conclusions were represented with existing atom kinds while preserving the source as a secondary synthesis.

Trial-sequential-analysis required-information-size statements do not map cleanly to QuantitativeResult's comparative population/exposure/outcome structure; they were retained as 'other' atoms rather than forced into an inappropriate quantitative-result context.
source_gaps: The selected materials folder contains only the primary PDF. The article's data-availability statement refers to article/supplementary material, but no separate supplementary file was present for review.
